Predicates for search expressions
Predicate	Description
after			date format is RFC3339, but can be shortened as required.
i.e. 2011-01-01 is Jan 1 of year 2011 and "2011" means the same.
before			date format is RFC3339, but can be shortened as required.
i.e. 2011-01-01 is Jan 1 of year 2011 and "2011" means the same.
attr			match on attribute. Use attr:foo:bar to match nodes having their foo
attribute set to bar or attr:foo:~bar to do a substring
case-insensitive search for 'bar' in attribute foo
childrenof		Find child permanodes of a parent permanode (or prefix of a parent
permanode): childrenof:sha1-527cf12 Only matches permanodes currently.
parentof		Find parent permanodes of a child permanode (or prefix of a child
permanode): parentof:sha1-527cf12 Only matches permanodes currently.
format			file's format (or MIME-type) such as jpg, pdf, tiff.
tag			match on a tag
title			match nodes containing substring in their title
ref			match nodes whose blobRef starts with the given substring
camera			Match EXIF camera make or model, case insensitively. Supports '*' at either end, or '~' for substring matching.
is:image		object is an image
is:livephoto		object is the still image of a Live Photo whose video is indexed
is:livephotovideo	object is the video of a Live Photo whose still image is indexed
livephoto		Match both halves of the Live Photo with the given Apple content identifier, case insensitively.
height			use height:min-max to match images having a height of at least min
and at most max. Use height:min- to specify only an underbound and
height:-max to specify only an upperbound.
Exact matches should use height:480
is:landscape		the image has a landscape aspect
is:pano			the image's aspect ratio is over 2 - panorama picture.
is:portrait		the image has a portrait aspect
width			use width:min-max to match images having a width of at least min
and at most max. Use width:min- to specify only an underbound and
width:-max to specify only an upperbound.
Exact matches should use width:640
filename		Match filename, case sensitively. Supports optional '*' wildcard at beginning, end, or both.
is:post			matches tweets, status updates, blog posts, etc
is:like			matches liked tweets
is:checkin		matches location check-ins (foursquare, etc)
is:bookmark		matches bookmarks (raindrop.io, pinboard, etc)
is:untagged		matches untagged permanodes
is:fitness		matches all fitnessActivity permanodes, including unknown sports and activities without GPS.
is:run			matches fitness activities classified as run.
is:hike			matches fitness activities classified as hike.
is:ride			matches fitness activities classified as ride, including mountain, gravel, virtual, and electric cycling.
is:bike			alias for is:ride; includes all cycling subtypes, including electric bikes.
is:ebike		matches fitness rides whose Strava sport is EBikeRide or EMountainBikeRide; uses legacy stravaActivityType only when stravaSportType is absent or empty.

miles			matches fitness activity distance in miles; use >=5, <=5, >5, <5, =5 or 5, and inclusive ranges 5-10, 5-, -10. Values must be nonnegative finite decimal numbers (scientific notation allowed); miles are 1609.344 meters.

km			matches fitness activity distance in km; use >=5, <=5, >5, <5, =5 or 5, and inclusive ranges 5-10, 5-, -10. Values must be nonnegative finite decimal numbers (scientific notation allowed); miles are 1609.344 meters.

kilometers		alias for km; matches fitness activity distance in kilometers; use >=5, <=5, >5, <5, =5 or 5, and inclusive ranges 5-10, 5-, -10. Values must be nonnegative finite decimal numbers (scientific notation allowed); miles are 1609.344 meters.

meters			matches fitness activity distance in meters; use >=5, <=5, >5, <5, =5 or 5, and inclusive ranges 5-10, 5-, -10. Values must be nonnegative finite decimal numbers (scientific notation allowed); miles are 1609.344 meters.
has:location		matches images and permanodes that have a location (GPSLatitude
and GPSLongitude can be retrieved from the image's EXIF tags).
loc			matches images and permanodes having a location near
the specified location.  Locations are resolved using
maps.googleapis.com. For example: loc:"new york, new york"
locrect			matches images and permanodes having a location within
the specified location area. The area is defined by its
North-West corner, followed and comma-separated by its
South-East corner. Each corner is defined by its latitude,
followed and comma-separated by its longitude.
with			match people containing substring in their first or last name
